title: Runtime kernel selection drift — incident review and runbook draft
summary: During a gradual rollout of v3.1.0 of the serving runtime, a subset of canary hosts began selecting a non-optimized kernel path for long-sequence requests. The change increased 95th percentile latency for those hosts by ~3.2x and caused intermittent request timeouts. This doc captures the detection, investigation, immediate mitigations, and proposed runbook changes to prevent recurrence.
impact: Approximately 7% of production inference capacity (multi-tenant pool eu-west-2a) experienced elevated tail latency and ~0.6% increased error rates for generative endpoints for the 90-minute window. No data loss. Several customer requests experienced degraded UX (timeouts / slow streaming).
detection: Alerting fired from SLO-monitoring: streaming-p99 > 650ms on route /v1/generate for eu-west-2a. Pager duty rotation responded. Initial hypothesis called out model weights or KV cache; tracing showed kernels used differed from expected profile.
timeline:
2025-09-09 02:04 UTC - rollout of runtime v3.1.0 started (staged by region)
2025-09-09 02:37 UTC - first p99 alerts for /v1/generate in eu-west-2a
2025-09-09 02:42 UTC - oncall triage: checked canary dashboards, confirmed latency spike localized to subset of hosts
2025-09-09 03:05 UTC - correlation with kernel-selection logs: hosts reported fallback to generic_attention kernel instead of fused_attention_v2
2025-09-09 03:20 UTC - temporary traffic shift off affected hosts (routing policy) reduced customer impact
2025-09-09 03:40 UTC - rollback of v3.1.0 on affected node pool initiated
2025-09-09 04:10 UTC - metrics returned to baseline; incident declared mitigated
2025-09-12 09:00 UTC - preliminary RCA review with infra and runtime teams
investigation_notes:
- Kernel-selection logic change in v3.1.0 introduced a heuristic that prefers fused_attention_v2 only when kernel_signature matches exact config (seq_len_bucket, head_dim, quantization flag).
- A recent maintenance change to the kernel metadata generation (build-time) added a minor ordering difference in kernel metadata JSON; heuristics compare string keys and failed to identify the fused kernel as compatible.
- The ordering drift was introduced by build-tooling bump (bazel rules -> 3.8.1) which changed deterministic JSON output order for our kernel manifest in a tiny subset of images.
- Hosts with older kernel-catalog cache entries kept an older manifest and matched correctly; hosts that pulled the new manifest saw mismatched signatures and fell back to generic path.
- Repro locally by generating kernel manifest with new toolchain and running kernel-matcher: fallback observed for model configs with seq_len > 1024.
root_cause: Configuration and build-tooling drift changed kernel manifest ordering such that the kernel signature comparator (string-ordered) failed to recognize compatible optimized kernels. Combined with a brittle comparator implementation (string comparison rather than normalized structural compare) caused the runtime to select slower fallback kernels.
immediate_mitigations:
- Rerouted traffic away from affected node pool (automated routing policy)
- Rolled back runtime v3.1.0 on affected pool images to v3.0.7 (which used previous manifest output)
- Invalidated kernel-catalog cache on all hosts and forced a rebuild of manifest with a normalization step on a small cohort to confirm behavior before reintroducing images
- Short-term customer comms: notified affected internal stakeholders and Customer Success for a small set of high-traffic tenants
rollback_steps:
1) Mark node pool in cluster-manager as do-not-deploy
2) Trigger image rollback job for pool to v3.0.7 (ID: img-3.0.7-202508)
3) Force eviction and drain nodes gracefully (drain timeout 5m)
4) Confirm kernel-selection logs show fused_attention_v2 selected
5) Monitor p99 and error rates for 30m before removing do-not-deploy flag
remediation_plan:
- Replace string-based kernel signature comparator with a normalized structural comparator (ignore ordering, canonicalize keys) - tracked in GH PR #4723
- Update build-tooling to emit sorted keys (defensive) as an interim compatibility guarantee
- Add manifest schema version and checksum to runtime bootstrap to detect incompatible manifest formats early
- Expand canary checks: add a kernel-selection smoke test that runs a short long-seq inference (seq_len 2048) on canary hosts and validates selected kernel path before shifting traffic
long_term_mitigation:
- Harden build/release pipeline: add a manifest-compatibility gate in release CI (Jenkins pipeline step)
- Add automated delta detection for kernel manifest diffs and require sign-off for changes that alter selection-relevant fields
- Implement a runtime feature flag to allow safe progressive enablement of kernel heuristics per-pool
- Document kernel manifest format and comparator expectations in internal runtime design doc
monitoring_changes:
- New metric: runtime.kernel.selection_mismatch_count (tagged by pool, kernel_name)
- New alert: if > 3 selection_mismatch_count events in 5m for a single pool -> P2
- Add canary smoke-test result to rollout dashboard with green/red tile and block rollout if red
runbook_updates:
Draft runbook entries to be added:
- 'Kernel manifest mismatch triage' section with quick-check commands (kubectl, curl to local manifest endpoint, logs query examples)
- 'Quick rollback' checklist that explicitly marks cache invalidation as a step
- 'Build toolchain rollback' playbook for infra when manifest format changes detected
sla_impact: Minor customer-visible degradation for limited tenants for ~90 minutes. No SLA credits expected but monitor for downstream escalations.
lessons_learned:
- Small build-tooling changes can have outsized runtime impact when format assumptions are brittle.
- Unit tests that assert deterministic JSON ordering are brittle; instead assert semantic equality.
- Canary checks must include behavior-level smoke tests (not just health endpoints).
- Release owners need a preflight checklist that verifies manifest compatibility across historical runtimes.
next_steps:
- Merge GH PR #4723 (normalized comparator) and roll out to a small canary pool with smoke test
- Add manifest checksum gate to release CI by 2025-09-20 (JIRA: ENGOPS-2191)
- Update runbook and push to Confluence; schedule a 30-minute training with oncall rotations
- Re-run incident blameless postmortem on 2025-09-16 with infra and runtime teams
status_summary: Mitigated (rollback + traffic shift). Fix in progress: comparator change in review. Runbook draft created — pending approvals from runtime and infra owners.
